title: Dynamic legacy item redirects can corrupt IDs containing reserved URL characters
reasoning: SvelteKit route params are decoded before being passed to load. Interpolating params.id directly into a redirect URL can turn reserved characters such as '/', '?', or '#' into path/query/fragment syntax instead of preserving them as the item identifier. A legacy URL like /podcasts/items/a%2Fb can redirect to /sources/media/items/a/b rather than /sources/media/items/a%2Fb, changing the target resource or producing a 404.
reproduction: Request /podcasts/items/a%2Fb or /youtube/items/a%3Fb and observe that the Location header is built from the decoded parameter instead of an encoded path segment.
recommendation: Encode the dynamic path segment when constructing the redirect target, for example `/sources/media/items/${encodeURIComponent(params.id)}`.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for these frontend route redirects, and there is no evidence of coverage for encoded or reserved-character item IDs.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a SvelteKit route/load test or Playwright test asserting that /podcasts/items/a%2Fb and /youtube/items/a%2Fb redirect to /sources/media/items/a%2Fb.
minimumFixScope: Update both dynamic item redirect load functions to encode params.id and add focused redirect coverage for reserved-character IDs.
